Give indicators processes of their own

Source: R/ctModelUniqueProcess.R
ctModelUniqueProcess.Rd

Each manifest variable in items gets a latent, named u_ and the variable's name, that loads only on that variable with a fixed loading of one, and has its own persistence and innovations. The variable then has, besides what it shares with others through the model's latents and its measurement error, a specific part that persists over time. This suits an item whose wording picks up something besides the construct, consistently over time.

Usage

ctModelUniqueProcess(ctm, items, shared = FALSE, name = NULL)

Arguments

ctm

A model from ctModel(type = 'ct').

items

Which manifest variables, by name or position.

shared

If TRUE, one process for all of items, named u_ and their names joined by _, instead of one each.

name

Names for the new latents, replacing the defaults: one for a shared process, otherwise one per item. Useful for adding a second process on the same items at another time scale.

Value

The extended model.

Details

Without such a process, the specific part can only go into the measurement error, which is independent over time, or into the shared latents, whose dynamics it then distorts. In the first case the item's prediction errors stay correlated over nearby times, which the residuals family of ctFitAdequacy shows. The specific process and the measurement error are distinguished by persistence over time.

The process has no intercept (the item's own intercept carries its level), ctsem's default drift transform, so it is mean reverting, and innovations independent of the other latents. It starts from its stationary distribution, with mean zero and the variance its persistence and innovations imply (the T0VAR diagonal 'stationary', see ctFit).

With shared = TRUE the items share one process, with a loading of one on the first item and free loadings on the others, representing what moves them together beyond the model's other latents. Measurement errors that are correlated within an occasion are often better modelled this way, as a process faster than the occasions, unless the design gives a reason for correlated error, such as a method shared by the items.

See also

ctModelImprove, which adds one for the items the adequacy check points to.

Examples

m <- ctModel(type = 'ct', manifestNames = c('Y1', 'Y2', 'Y3'),
  latentNames = 'eta', LAMBDA = matrix(c(1, 'l2', 'l3'), 3))
m2 <- ctModelUniqueProcess(m, 'Y2')
m2$latentNames
p <- m2$pars
p[p$col %in% 2 & p$matrix %in% c('LAMBDA', 'DRIFT', 'DIFFUSION'),
  c('matrix', 'row', 'col', 'param', 'value')]
ctModelUniqueProcess(m, c('Y2', 'Y3'), shared = TRUE)$latentNames
